review_scope: Read-only source and retained builder control audit; no invocation of collector, no remote calls or graph workload, no script edits

checks.result: Selects inspect ID/init PID/running, top pid/ppid/comm and explicit proc status whitelist; no cmdline or environ reads.

Proc stat field22 starttime parsed correctly after final parenthesis. Full container ID checked against cgroup; before/after start_ticks rejects detected PID replacement during one row read. Disappearance, permission and parse errors retained per row.
Exclusive-create receipt prevents overwrite. Full ID pins top after name lookup. Reader only opens proc files, does not signal or write target cell; benchmark source and sampler remain unchanged.
VM monotonic bounds and SC_CLK_TCK retained for timing/starttime interpretation; status NSpid supplies observed host/container namespace identifiers.

limits: The process list and each row are sequential observations, not an atomic container snapshot. Processes born after docker top are omitted.

Reuse between docker top and the first stat read within the same container is not detected; mapping describes the process alive at the proc read, and status Name/PPid should take precedence over earlier top fields.

Container ID persists across restart. Initial inspect PID is not revalidated after capture; no boot_id or PID-namespace inode is recorded. Do not stitch samples across an unverified VM/container restart.
Start ticks reduce in-read reuse ambiguity but are clock-tick resolution and do not establish continuity after capture. The cgroup is read once, not rechecked after status.

Outer outcome captured means the helper completed, not that every process mapped. Callers must check per-row errors, presence/shape of NSpid, host PID consistency and full cgroup identity; the script itself does not require these successful-row invariants.
Three successful builder mappings qualify diagnostic plumbing only; they do not demonstrate Sail worker behavior or identify any historical OOM victim.
future_oom_attribution: A successful row directly observes host-PID to namespace-PID mapping at capture. A future worker OOM attribution must also match full cgroup and same-boot kernel event host PID, connect the namespace PID to the worker startup/identity record, and use nearby/repeated captures or lifecycle evidence to exclude intervening PID reuse/restart. A single early mapping is not permanent worker identity; remaining continuity uncertainty must remain explicit.
optional_hardening: A future version could record boot_id and PID namespace inode, revalidate init/cgroup at capture end, and distinguish complete/partial mapping outcomes; no change made in this audit.
